subject: CI for std.all latent change model - model fit?

messages.author: 36893a47af4252c6
messages.subject: CI for std.all latent change model - model fit?
parts:
Dear all,

we have the following problem: we estimated (very complex)!) neighborhood latent change models.
For the latent correlations (std.all coefficient) between the difference variables we calculated the 95% CIs.
We estimated the CFA (SEM-) Model with std.lv =TRUE and summary ci =TRUE to get the CIs.

This worked very well, however the prior good model fit changed and the model does not fit anymore (furthermore, the df changed, even if we did not change the specified model).

How can this be and how can we get the correct CIs for the standardized coefficients (latent correlations of difference values)?

Thanks for any helpful advice!
S.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: CI for std.all latent change model - model fit?
parts: the df changed, even if we did not change the specified model

You can inspect the parTable() output of both models to see what changed.  Not sure what purpose std.lv = TRUE would serve here, unless you are looking at latent difference scores in latent variables, which gets very tricky.  Also see a recent discussion started on SEMNET about whether standardized estimates are even valid for latent difference scores, since they are standardized relative to variable components having variances of 1 rather than actual variables. 

https://listserv.ua.edu/cgi-bin/wa?A2=ind1706&L=semnet&F=&S=&P=81902

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

On 06/08/2017 08:18 PM, Simona wrote:
> how can we get the correct CIs for the standardized
> coefficients

The dev version of lavaan (0.6.1) shows (simple symmetric) CIs in the
output of standardizedSolution().

You can install it by typing in R:

install.packages("lavaan", repos = "http://www.da.ugent.be", type =
"source")

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: CI for std.all latent change model - model fit?
parts: maybe this is all ok

No, "non-zero exit status" means there was a problem that prevented installation.  The top line with the ERROR message tells you what the problem was.  You can install the dependency in a fresh R session, then try again:

install.packages("numDeriv")
install.packages("lavaan", repos="http://www.da.ugent.be", type="source")
